# synapserutils

```{=gfm}
> [!WARNING]
> **This package is deprecated and no longer maintained.** Its functions are now built into [`synapser`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/) 3.0 and later, so you no longer need a separate package. See the [synapser documentation](https://r-docs.synapse.org/) and the [migration guide for synapser 3.0](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/articles/migration_to_synapser_3_0.html).
```

`synapserutils` only works with `synapser` 2.x. It can't be installed alongside `synapser` 3.0.

## Where each function went

In `synapser` 3.0, these utilities are methods you call on a `File`, `Folder`, `Project`, or `WikiPage`, usually with a pipe. For example, `copy("syn123", "syn456")` becomes `File(id = "syn123") |> synCopy(parent_id = "syn456")`.

| `synapserutils` | `synapser` 3.0 replacement |
|---|---|
| `copy()` | `synCopy()` on a [`File`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/File_Copy.html), [`Folder`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/Folder_Copy.html), or [`Project`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/Project_Copy.html) |
| `copyWiki()` | `synCopy()` on a [`WikiPage`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/WikiPage_Copy.html) |
| `syncFromSynapse()` | [`synSyncFromSynapse()`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/Folder_SyncFromSynapse.html) on a `Folder` or `Project`. See [Downloading data in bulk](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/articles/download_data_in_bulk.html). |
| `syncToSynapse()` | [`synSyncToSynapse()`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/Folder_SyncToSynapse.html) on a `Folder` or `Project`. See [Uploading data in bulk](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/articles/upload_data_in_bulk.html). |
| `generate_sync_manifest()` | [`synGenerateSyncManifest()`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/Folder_GenerateSyncManifest.html) on a `Folder` or `Project` |
| `walk()` | [`synWalk()`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/Folder_Walk.html) on a `Folder` or `Project` |
| `changeFileMetaData()` | [`synChangeMetadata()`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/File_ChangeMetadata.html) on a `File` |
| `generateManifest()` | No direct replacement. `synSyncFromSynapse()` writes a `manifest.csv` for you. See [Manifest CSV](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/articles/manifest_csv.html). |
| `copyFileHandles()` | No direct replacement. Call the [`POST /filehandles/copy`](https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/POST/filehandles/copy.html) REST endpoint with [`synRestPost()`](https://r-docs.synapse.org/v3.0.0/reference/synRestPost.html). |

## Legacy documentation (synapser 2.x)

The rest of this page describes the last release of `synapserutils` (1.2.0) and is kept for anyone still using `synapser` 2.x.

The `synapserutils` package provides a set of utility functions, built on top of the `synapser` package.

### Installation

`synapserutils` is available as a ready-built package for Microsoft Windows and Mac OSX. For Linux systems, it is available to install from source. It can be installed or upgraded using the standard `install.packages()` command, adding the [Sage Bionetworks R Archive Network (RAN)](http://ran.synapse.org) to the repository list, e.g.:

```{r eval=F}
install.packages("synapserutils", repos=c("http://ran.synapse.org", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```
Alternatively, edit your `~/.Rprofile` and configure your default repositories:
```{r eval=F}
options(repos=c("http://ran.synapse.org", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```
after which you may run `install.packages` without specifying the repositories:
```{r eval=F}
install.packages("synapserutils")
```

If you have been asked to validate a release candidate, please replace the URL https://sage-bionetworks.github.io/ran with https://sage-bionetworks.github.io/staging-ran, that is:

```{r eval=F}
install.packages("synapserutils", repos=c("http://staging-ran.synapse.org", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

### Usage

To get started, try logging into Synapse. If you don't already have a Synapse account, register [here](https://www.synapse.org/register):

```{r eval=F}
library(synapserutils)
synLogin()
```

### Available Utilities

#### Copy

##### Copy Entity (File, Folder, Table, Link, and Project)

The example below copies File ID `syn123` to Project ID `syn456`:
```{r eval=F}
copy("syn123", "syn456")
```

The first parameter in `copy()` can be a File ID, a Table ID, or a Link ID. The second parameter must be a Folder ID or a Project ID.

For more information on `copy()`, please see:
```{r eval=F}
?copy
```

##### Copy Wiki and Wiki Subpage

To copy a wiki page that is associated with an Entity (Project/ File/ Folder/ Table) `syn123` to another Entity `syn789`:
```{r eval=F}
copyWiki("syn123", "syn789")
```

For more information on `copyWiki()`, please see:
```{r eval=F}
?copyWiki
```

#### Batch Process

##### Upload Data in Bulk

`syncToSynapse()` takes a manifest file and uploads the files listed in the manifest file to Synapse:
```{r eval=F}
syncToSynapse("/path/to/manifest.tsv")
```

The manifest file format and instructions on how to create one can be found [here](http://docs.synapse.org/articles/uploading_in_bulk.html#creating-a-manifest) and by:
```{r eval=F}
?syncToSynapse
```

##### Download Data in Bulk

To recursively download all files within a container (Folder/ Project) `syn123`:
```{r eval=F}
syncFromSynapse("syn123")
```

More information on downloading data in bulk is available [here](http://docs.synapse.org/articles/uploading_in_bulk.html#downloading-data-in-bulk) and by:
```{r eval=F}
?syncFromSynapse
```

#### Other Utilites

To recursively getting Entity (File/ Folder/ Table/ Link/ Project) metadata from a container (Folder/ Project):
```{r eval=F}
walk("syn123")
```

For more information about `walk()`, please see:
```{r eval=F}
?walk
```
